notes: Updates that arrived while a song was playing are no longer thrown away. A launch defers the install to "when you close the app" so the music is never cut off — but that deferral was recorded as if the hand-over had happened, so the version’s single automatic attempt was burnt and it was never auto-installed again. The update stayed downloaded while the app kept opening the old build, which is why a fix could ship, install, and still change nothing on screen. A deferral now leaves the attempt unspent so the next launch installs it

A deferred install is no longer mistaken for a failed one. The record that tells the next boot "we handed the app over to this version, check it came up" was written even when nothing had been handed over, so the very next launch marked a perfectly good update as rolled back and refused it for good

Install now installs. The sheet’s button ran the same music-playing deferral as the automatic paths, so on a phone that always has something playing it hid the sheet and did nothing — the one manual escape hatch from a stuck update. It hands the bundle over immediately now; the sheet says the app is about to reopen, so stopping playback is the thing you just asked for

The update sheet tells you which build you are actually on (’You are on v58.9.8 → installing v58.9.9’). The version picker can leave an older page pinned over a newer installed bundle, and then every report of "it is still broken" is about the old page rather than the update being offered
